contests.title: Issue 3 — Proposed Constitutional Amendment TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE

provenance.quote: Shall the Charter of the City of Akron be amended to enact Section 101b so as to require property owners or operators to permit security deposits for residential rentals to be paid over three or six month periods; to require operators to inform tenants or prospective tenants of their right to make security deposit payments over three or six months; criminalizing the failure to provide the notification; banning fees, charges, deposits or other payments prior to executing rental agreements for residential rental properties; and criminalizing the collection of an application fee for residential rentals?

Shall the Charter of the City of Akron be amended to enact Section 100a to add the City of Akron's existing codified anti-discrimination protections in the Charter; to, with exceptions for sex offenders and arson offenders, prohibit owners and operators from declining to rent to, or engage in real estate transaction with, an individual on the basis of that individual's criminal history such as arrests, convictions, incarceration; making individuals with criminal histories a protected class similar to race, gender, sexual orientation, and other existing protected classes as it relates to renting, home sales, and other real estate transactions; giving Akron Civil Rights Commission jurisdiction over all real estate discrimination claims arising in Akron; and requiring City Council to enact implementing legislation within ninety (90) days of the effective date of this amendment?

Shall Section 68a of the Charter of the City of Akron be amended to change the composition and board member-appointment process of the citizen's police oversight board by reducing the number of members appointed by City Council and requiring the Board to select one-third of its own members from a preselected list provided by a committee comprised of individuals who are members of a "qualifying civil rights organization"; to establish procedures and timing requirements for the Mayor, Chief of Police, and City Council to respond to recommendations made by the Office of the Independent Police Auditor; to explicitly authorize the Office of the Independent Police Auditor to issue subpoenas compelling production of records in the possession of public or private entities or individuals; and to authorize the Office of Independent Police Auditor to compel attendance and testimony from private citizens and public employees?

contests.title: Columbus Issue 8 — City Council District Elections (By Petition)

provenance.quote: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. The amendment specifies that ballots within council districts will include both citywide races as well as the district race. The amendment allows for the initiation of a recall election of a council district representative if a petition is submitted bearing the signatures of the electors of that district in an amount that is at least fifteen (15%) percent of the votes cast within the district in the preceding mayoral election. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

measures.questionText:
Proposed Constitutional Amendment
TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO
IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE
Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly
To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution
of the State of Ohio
A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5.
This proposed amendment would:
• Require voters to present an approved form of government-
issued photo identification in order to vote.
• Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of
verifying a voter’s identity for a voter who has a sincere
religious objection to being photographed and, therefore,
does not possess an approved form of government-issued
photo identification.
• Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an
approved form of government-issued photo identification,
unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a
signature and at least one other specified unique identifier.
• Define approved forms of government-issued photo
identification as an unexpired Ohio driver license or state
identification card; a United States passport or passport card;
or a United States military identification card, Ohio National
Guard identification card, or United States Department of
Veterans Affairs identification card.
If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately.
A “YES” vote means approval of the amendment.
A “NO” vote means disapproval of the amendment.
SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires approved photo ID for in-person voting, while allowing state law to provide another identity check for voters who lack photo ID because of a sincere religious objection to being photographed. For voting by mail or another permitted method, requires photo ID or, if state law allows, a signature and another approved unique identifier: a government-assigned number or code, or a shortened version. Approved IDs include Ohio driver’s licenses or state ID cards, qualifying temporary state ID documents, U.S. passports or passport cards, and U.S. military, Ohio National Guard or Veterans Affairs IDs. All must be unexpired and include the voter’s name and photo.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve constitutional photo-ID requirements, effective immediately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires landlords to let tenants pay residential security deposits over three or six months and notify tenants and prospective tenants of that option. Makes failing to provide that notice a crime. Prohibits residential rental application fees and other fees, charges, deposits or payments before a rental agreement is signed, and makes collecting an application fee a crime.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Add these rental-payment requirements and penalties to Akron’s charter.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds the city’s existing anti-discrimination protections to Akron’s charter and generally bars refusing to rent or enter a real-estate transaction because of a person’s criminal history, with exceptions for sex offenders and arson offenders. Gives the Akron Civil Rights Commission authority over all real-estate discrimination claims arising in Akron and requires City Council to adopt implementing legislation within 90 days of the amendment taking effect.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Add these anti-discrimination provisions to Akron’s charter.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes how Akron’s civilian police oversight board is chosen: City Council would appoint fewer members, and the board would select one-third of its members from a list supplied by a committee of members of a qualifying civil-rights organization. Sets procedures and deadlines for the mayor, police chief and City Council to respond to the Independent Police Auditor’s recommendations. Authorizes the auditor to subpoena records held by public or private entities or individuals and compel attendance and testimony from private citizens and public employees.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these changes to the oversight board and police auditor’s powers.
